773.01. Permit required.
   No public vehicle shall be operated in the City of Toledo, except those
meeting one of the exemptions defined in Toledo Municipal Code
Chapter 769, unless a permit as either a taxicab or a motor vehicle for hire/
limousine has been issued for such vehicle and is in force.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
773.02. Application for a permit.
   Applications for permits shall be made to the Board of Review upon blanks
provided by the Director and shall set forth the name and address of the
applicant, the trade name under which he, she or it does business, the class of
vehicle (taxicab or motor vehicle for hire/limousine) for which the permit is
desired, the seating capacity, the design, the color scheme and lettering and
marks to be used on such vehicle and any other information required by the
Director. Applicants for permits must meet all qualifications set forth in
Toledo Municipal Code Section
775.01 for applications for City operating licenses except those listed in
Section
775.01(e).
   Applications for, and renewals of, a motor vehicle for hire/limousine permit
must include written verification of the applicant's current registration with
the Public Utilities Commission of Ohio ("PUCO") as an intrastate passenger
carrier and also the applicant's current United States Department of
Transportation ("USDOT") registration number. In lieu of a USDOT registration
number, an applicant may provide a notarized affidavit certifying that the
applicant is not subject to USDOT regulation because none of applicant's
business crosses state lines. No new or renewal permit for a motor vehicle for
hire/limousine shall be issued without this registration verification.
   Under no circumstances shall permits be issued to an individual or company
that does not reasonably expect to have the permitted vehicle on the road and
being driven by the permit holder or his employee within sixty (60) days. Under
no circumstances shall a permit application be granted to any applicant who
currently has one or more permits under revocation for a reason other than non-
use. Permits shall not be issued in anticipation of transfer to others. If the
application is granted, the applicant shall furnish to the Director prior to
issuance or renewal of the permit information to include the make and model,
the state license number, the name and address of the owner of the vehicle, a
list of all persons who will be operating the permitted vehicle and any other
information required by the Director. All vehicles shall display any license
plate and/or sticker as required by the State of Ohio.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
773.03. Issuance of taxicab and motor vehicle for hire/limousine permits.
   The Board of Review shall investigate and hold a hearing as to each
applicant for a permit for a taxicab or motor vehicle for hire/limousine. Such
hearings shall be held at least quarterly each year. All applications to be
considered at each hearing must be on file at the City of Toledo Central Permit
Center at least five (5) full business days before the hearing. If the Board of
Review finds from its investigation and hearing that the applicant has not made
false statements on the application, is not addicted to the use of alcohol or
drugs, has obtained satisfactory criminal record checks as required by
Chapter 775 of this Public Vehicle Code and has provided satisfactory
confirmation of State and federal registration or exemption as required by
Section
773.02, and/or finds that the public convenience and necessity justify the
operation of the vehicle for which the permit is desired, the Board shall
notify forthwith the applicant of its finding. Within sixty (60) days
thereafter, the applicant shall furnish the Officer with all additional
information required and, if the Director then finds that such vehicle is a
safe and fit conveyance and that it complies with all the requirements of this
Public Vehicle Code, he shall notify the Division of Taxation & Treasury, which
shall issue a permit to the applicant upon payment of the proper permit fee and
the furnishing of the required bond or insurance.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
773.04. Notice of adverse finding.
   If the Board of Review finds from such investigation and hearing that the
public convenience and necessity do not justify the operation of the vehicle
for which the permit is so desired, it shall forthwith notify the applicant of
its finding.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
773.05. Permit fee and term.
   Every permit shall expire on April 30 of each year. Except as hereinafter
provided, the permit fee for each public vehicle shall be in the sum of one
hundred dollars ($100.00), payable to the Division of Taxation & Treasury, such
sum payable annually for each year for which same is issued. The initial permit
fee for any new permit issued between January 1st and April 30th shall be
reduced to fifty dollars ($50.00) to cover the remainder of the current license
year. Any permit fee indicated by this section shall be in addition to any fee
required under the laws of the State for all motor vehicles. Any permit not
renewed by April 30 shall be subject to a surcharge in the amount of ten
dollars ($10.00). The permit fee shall be waived for any motor vehicle for
hire/limousine large enough to be subject to PUCO certification requirements
for mechanical safety and roadworthiness if written evidence of compliance with
such PUCO requirements is provided to the Officer. The Officer shall not be
required to perform a vehicle safety inspection for vehicles qualifying for
this fee waiver. Subject to all other requirements of this Public Vehicle Code,
a permit will still be issued for, and must be displayed on, any motor vehicle
for hire/limousine qualifying for the fee waiver.
   Notwithstanding the foregoing, there shall be a minimum annual fee of two
hundred dollars ($200.00) assessed to any person or business entity operating
motor vehicles for hire/limousines that qualify for the aforementioned fee
waiver. Permit fees paid by the same person or business entity for one or more
motor vehicles for hire/limousines not qualifying for the fee waiver shall be
counted toward the minimum annual fee.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
773.06. Assignment of metal tags and body numbers.
   (a)   At the time the permit is issued by the Officer for any public
vehicle, there shall also be issued to the owner of such permit either a
sticker or a metal tag showing the class of public vehicle, the license number
and the year for which issued. The sticker or tag for each class of public
vehicle shall be numbered consecutively each year, and the numbers on such tag
shall correspond with the permit numbers, which shall in turn correspond with a
body number assigned by the Officer, except as provided in Section 773.07.
   (b)   If at any time a permit is suspended or revoked, the owner of the
permit shall remove from the vehicle or vehicles each identifying metal tag or
sticker and forthwith return each such tag or sticker to the Officer. In
addition, all identification, painting and lettering must be removed before the
vehicle may be operated on the public streets.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
773.07. When body numbers not assigned.
   Upon application, the Officer may issue a permit for a motor vehicle for
hire/limousine without assigning a body number when it is shown that the
vehicle for which the permit is desired is being used for livery purposes as a
motor vehicle for hire/limousine rather than as a taxicab.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
773.08. Vehicles to carry tags.
   No tag shall be displayed on any public vehicle except the one issued
specifically for that vehicle. The tag shall be affixed to the rear of the
vehicle so as to be plainly discernible at all times.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
773.09. Temporary permits.
   Any public vehicle owner holding at least one (1) current permit for either
a taxicab or a motor vehicle for hire/limousine may request up to five (5)
temporary permits of the same class as the current permit(s). Application for
temporary permits shall be made to the Board of Review in the same manner as
application for a regular permit.
   Issuance of temporary permits shall be contingent upon the availability of
sufficient permits within the maximum allowable number specified in Section
771.01 as well as upon meeting the same qualification requirements specified in
Section
773.03, including payment of all permit fees.
   A temporary permit shall be valid only until the next meeting of the Board
of Review. Conversion of a temporary permit to regular permanent status shall
be contingent upon the Board's approval.
   No temporary permit shall be issued to a public vehicle owner whose current
vehicle(s) operate under a business/trade name for which he/she is not the
rights holder unless written authorization for the issuance of a temporary
permit is given by the holder of the rights to the business/trade name to be
used.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
773.10. Identification, painting and lettering.
   Every person, firm, association or corporation owning and operating taxicabs
or motor vehicles for hire/limousines under permit from the City may adopt a
trade name, design, color scheme or method of painting or lettering such
taxicabs or motor vehicles for hire/limousines that is approved by the
Director. All taxicabs doing business under the same company name shall bear
consistent markings. Such trade name, design, color scheme or method of
painting or lettering shall include the following matter:
   (a)   A serial body number assigned by the Officer to each taxicab or motor
vehicle for hire/limousine and painted on each side of the taxicab or motor
vehicle for hire/limousine, except as provided in Section
773.07.
   (b)   The name of the owner or trade name under which he, she or it does
business painted on each side of a taxicab. Whenever the name of a taxicab
owner, or the trade name under which he, she or it does business, does not
include any one of the words "taxicab", "taxi", "cab", then the word "taxicab"
shall be painted on each side of the taxicab immediately beneath such name or
trade name. Motor vehicles for hire/limousines shall be required only to
display the name of the owner or trade name under which he, she or it does
business either on the sides or on the rear of the vehicle along with the City
of Toledo permit sticker.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
773.11. If approved trade name not adopted.
   Whenever any person, firm, association or corporation owning and operating
one or more taxicabs does not adopt and use an approved trade name, design,
color scheme or method of painting and lettering as hereinbefore mentioned,
then it shall be mandatory for such person, firm, association or corporation to
paint the following matter on each of its taxicabs whether or not using an
approved trade name, design, color scheme or method of painting or lettering as
hereinbefore mentioned:
   A framed panel on each side enclosing on separate lines the name of the
owner, the word "taxicab" and the serial body number assigned to the taxicab by
the Officer, and shall cover no less area than ten (10) inches by twelve (12)
inches. The form of such panel shall be substantially as follows:
   John T. Smith
   Taxicab
   320
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
773.12. Specifications for lettering.
   All mandatory lettering or wording, whether in a particular trade name,
design, color scheme, method of painting or lettering or otherwise, as
hereinbefore provided, shall be at least three (3) inches in height, and shall
be of such color as in the opinion of the Director will contrast distinctly
with the background color on the body of the taxicab or motor vehicle for hire/
limousine. Provided further that such serial body numbers on the sides shall be
no less than three (3) inches in height.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
773.13. Compliance.
   No person shall cause or permit any taxicab to appear with a trade name,
design, color scheme or method of painting or lettering that is not approved by
the Director for the vehicle concerned, or that is not in accordance with the
terms of this chapter.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
773.14. Transfer of permit from vehicle to vehicle.
   In the event that the vehicle for which a permit has been issued becomes
unsuitable for operation, an affidavit to such effect may be filed with the
Director and the Director shall thereupon notify the Officer who shall transfer
the permit to any other vehicle designated by the owner of such permit,
provided such vehicle is of the same class and approved by the Director.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
773.15. Transfer of permit from owner to owner.
   (a)   No permit for any public vehicle shall be transferred from one owner
to another by the Officer except after application to the Board of Review and a
finding by the Board of Review that such transfer will not be detrimental to
the public interest. Such finding shall be arrived at in the same manner as per
an original application, and the transferee of such permit shall comply with
all the terms and conditions of this Public Vehicle Code governing public
vehicles.
   (b)   Any owner of a permit who, in violation of this section, shall
transfer such permit without having first applied to and obtained the
permission of the Board of Review shall be ineligible to apply for a permit for
two (2) years after having so transferred such permit. This penalty shall be in
addition to the penalties provided in this chapter for violation of the
provisions of this chapter. Any permit so transferred in violation of this
section shall be automatically cancelled and shall upon such transfer be and
become forthwith null, void and invalid, and the operation of any vehicle under
such cancelled permit shall be unlawful, and subject to all applicable
penalties in this chapter specified. The transferee of such permit, receiving
such transfer in violation of this section, shall be ineligible to apply for a
permit for one (1) year following such illegal transfer.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
773.16. Notification of substitution or sale of vehicle.
   Every owner of a permit for a public vehicle shall notify the Director upon
the substitution or sale of such public vehicle.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
773.17. Renewals.
   All permits issued in accordance with the terms of this Chapter shall be
renewed for each succeeding year without further hearing by the Board of
Review, providing there is compliance with all other requirements of this
Public Vehicle Code.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
773.18. Revocation of permits.
   (a)   Non-use. Whenever any person, firm or corporation holding one or more
permits for taxicabs or motor vehicles for hire/limousines shall for a period
of sixty (60) consecutive days fail to make a reasonable and consistent effort
to operate any such taxicab or motor vehicle for hire/limousine, except on
account of an emergency over which the owner of the permit has no control, the
Board of Review may revoke the permit for such vehicle or vehicles; provided
that this section shall not apply in the case of permits which have been
suspended in accordance with the provisions of Section
773.18.
   (b)   Employment of unlicensed drivers. No holder of any taxicab or motor
vehicle for hire/limousine permit shall allow the permitted vehicle to be
driven for hire by anyone who does not possess a public vehicle operator's
license.
   (c)   Unsafe and unsanitary condition. Every public vehicle shall be kept in
a safe and sanitary operating condition, with the vehicle cleaned regularly
inside and out and maintained with a neat and clean appearance, including, but
not limited to, the presence of no visible body rust, no torn or ripped
interior surfaces and no missing parts. Whenever a public vehicle is found by
any law enforcement officer not to be in a neat, clean, safe and sanitary
operating condition, the Board of Review may suspend or revoke the permit of
such public vehicle.
   (d)   Unlawful use. Upon information that any unlawful use of a permitted
vehicle has occurred with the knowledge of the person holding the permit for
such public vehicle, or the knowledge of the operator of such vehicle, the
Board of Review may suspend or revoke the permit for the vehicle involved or
the public vehicle operator's license of the driver involved, or both.
   (e)   Misrepresentation in obtaining a permit or public vehicle operator's
license. Whenever it shall appear upon investigation and hearing by the Board
of Review that a permit or public vehicle operator's license issued hereunder
has been obtained by misrepresentation, the Board of Review may revoke such
license and/or permit.
   (f)   Improper or incorrect taximeter. Following a conviction for violation
of Section
783.15, it shall be mandatory for the Board of Review to revoke the permit of
the vehicle concerned.
   (g)   In the event that a law enforcement officer issues a citation for a
violation of this section, the officer may, in addition to any penalties
permitted by state or local law, tow and impound the vehicle pursuant to Toledo
Municipal Code §
303.08 or immobilize the vehicle at its current location and may
administratively revoke on a temporary basis the owner's permit until such time
of the next regular Board of Review meeting. Provided, however, that any owner
or company that has not had a previous temporary revocation whose permit is
temporarily revoked may petition the Board of Review to, for good cause shown,
hear the matter prior to its next regular meeting. Upon hearing by the Board of
Review, under circumstances where a vehicle is so driven, the Board of Review
may suspend or revoke the permit for the vehicle concerned.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
773.19. Escrowing of permits; voluntary.
   (a)   Any person holding one (1) or more permits for taxicabs or motor
vehicles for hire issued pursuant to the provisions of this chapter, may file
with the Board of Review an application for the holding in escrow of any number
of the permits held by the applicant. Application for such escrow shall be made
to the Board on blanks furnished by the Director and shall set forth such
information as may be required by the Board. The Board of Review shall conduct
an investigation and hold a hearing as to each application for the escrow of
permits. If the Board finds from such investigation and hearing that the public
convenience and necessity justify the escrow of all or a part of the permits
designated in the application, they shall forthwith notify the applicant, the
Director and the Officer indicating the permits as to which the application is
granted. The applicant shall thereupon deposit with the Officer all the metal
tags issued for the escrowed permits and shall be entitled to a certificate
from the Director certifying that the permits of the vehicles designated are
escrowed.
   (b)   No insurance or bond shall be required during the period for which the
escrow is in effect. During the time of escrow the permittee may sell or
otherwise dispose of any vehicle the permit of which has been duly escrowed.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
773.20. Resuming suspended permits.
   The holder of an escrowed permit, or the assignee of such holder, may at any
time apply to the Board of Review for the right to resume the use of such
escrowed permit. The applicant shall comply with all the provisions as in the
case of the renewal of a permit. If the Board of Review and the Director are
satisfied that all the provisions are complied with, the requisite metal tags
and body numbers shall be issued and assigned to the permittee in accordance
with Section
773.06 and the applicant shall again be permitted to operate the vehicle or
vehicles covered by the permits with the same privileges of renewal as attached
to such permit or permits prior to their being escrowed.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
773.21. Order to resume.
   If at any time the Board of Review determines that the public convenience
and necessity require the operation of one (1) or more escrowed permits, it
shall order the resumption of operation of a sufficient number of permits to
satisfy such public convenience and necessity. The order to resume operations
shall apply to the escrowed permits within the particular type of permit in the
order in which the applications for escrow were granted, that is, the permit
first suspended shall be the first as to which the order to resume is made. The
order to resume operation of a permit may be served personally or by mail to
the permittee at his address as filed with the Director. If a permittee fails
for a period of forty-five (45) days to resume operation after resumption has
been ordered by the Board of Review, the permit or permits affected by the
order shall be revoked.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
773.22. Scope.
   Nothing herein contained shall prevent a transfer of a permit from owner to
owner, as is provided in Section
773.14, or the transfer of the right to the renewal of a permit or permits for
vehicles under escrowed operation or their substitute as provided herein.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
773.23. Board of Review may make regulations.
   The Board of Review, in consultation with the Director of Public Safety, is
hereby authorized and empowered to establish and adopt such additional
procedural rules and regulations governing the issuance of permits for, and
licenses to drive, taxicabs and motor vehicles for hire/limousines, and for the
holding and conduct of their meetings, as may be reasonable and necessary and
not inconsistent with the provisions of this Public Vehicle Code. This
authority shall specifically include the ability to require renewing permit
holders to provide a sworn affidavit certifying that the permit holder has been
fully in compliance with all of the regulations and requirements of this Public
Vehicle Code for the prior license year as a prerequisite for renewal of a
permit.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
773.24. Business records.
   Upon demand by the Director or the Board of Review, the holder of a public
vehicle owner's permit shall provide such records of his or her or its business
activity as are necessary to verify compliance with the various requirements of
this Public Vehicle Code. The holder of a public vehicle owner's permit shall
maintain such records for a minimum of three (3) years.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
773.99. Penalty.
   (a)   Any person, firm or corporation operating or permitting to be operated
for hire, a vehicle without a permit shall be guilty of a misdemeanor of the
fourth degree. In the event of conviction, such person, firm or corporation
shall not thereafter be granted a permit for a period of three (3) months for
the first conviction and one (1) year for a subsequent conviction.
   (b)   Any person, firm or corporation or any owner, agent, employee or
driver of a public vehicle who violates any of the provisions of this chapter
for which no other fine and/or imprisonment is specified is guilty of a minor
misdemeanor.
   (c)   While in the course of enforcing any requirement of this Public
Vehicle Code, the Director or any Toledo Police Officer is authorized to effect
the towing, impounding or immobilization of any permitted vehicle or any
vehicle not displaying a permit that the Director or Officer believes to be
engaged in activity not in conformance with the requirements of this Public
Vehicle Code.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)

Ch. 777
775.01. License required; application for public vehicle operator's license.
   No person shall drive for hire a taxicab or motor vehicle for hire/limousine
until he/she has been issued a valid public vehicle operator's license. Every
applicant for a license as a driver of a public vehicle shall make application
to the Officer on forms to be supplied by the Officer. The application, which
must be sworn by the applicant, shall set forth that the applicant:
   (a)   Is a citizen or legal resident of the United States;
   (b)   Is in compliance with all provisions of the Ohio Revised Code
applicable to licensing as a driver and financial responsibility or insurance;
and is not under suspension of driving privileges in any state.
   (c)   Is able to speak, read and write the English language;
   (d)   Is eighteen (18) years of age or over; provided, however, that no one
under the age of twenty-one (21) years shall be permitted to operate a taxicab
between the hours of midnight and 6:00 a.m.;
   (e)   Is free from defective vision, defective hearing, epilepsy, vertigo,
heart trouble and any other infirmity, physical or mental, which would render
him unfit for safe operation of a public vehicle;
   (f)   Is not addicted to the use of alcohol or drugs;
   (g)   Has or has not been convicted of a felony or of a misdemeanor
involving controlled substances or any sex offense (including public indecency)
or moral turpitude; and
   (h)   Is consenting to and will obtain a criminal record check from all
communities in which he has resided within the past ten (10) years; such other
pertinent information as the Director may require.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
775.02. Physician's certificate required.
   The application form shall further contain the certificate of a reputable
physician of Toledo (accompanied by such documentation as is required by the
Director) that the applicant is free from infirmities, dependencies or
addictions which would prevent his driving a public conveyance with safety; and
also setting forth the applicant's condition as to visual acuity, field of
vision and other vision together with a statement that the applicant has no eye
condition which would prevent his driving a public conveyance with safety.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
775.03. Examination of applicant.
   In addition to complying with the provisions of Sections
775.01 through
775.03, inclusive, every applicant may be examined by the Director or by an
inspector or deputy under his direction as to his knowledge of the laws and
provisions governing the operation of taxicabs or motor vehicles for hire/
limousines and as to his knowledge of the City and its traffic regulations. The
applicant shall produce evidence that he has had at least six (6) months'
experience in operating a motor vehicle and shall, if required, demonstrate his
skill and ability.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
775.04. Issuance of license.
   If the Director is satisfied that an applicant is a suitable and proper
person to drive a public vehicle, he shall notify the Officer in writing and
the Officer shall issue a license to the applicant upon payment of the proper
fee. The issuance of said license shall be deemed a Police Department function
and all applicable police record and character checks shall be consented to by
the applicant. Any individual administratively denied a license may appeal that
denial to the Board of Review. Provided, however, that the Board shall not
entertain appeals of persons convicted of sex offenses.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
775.05. Public vehicle operator's license fee.
   Every driver of a public vehicle shall pay to the Division of Taxation &
Treasury a license fee of twenty-five dollars ($25.00) per year for an original
license and a fee of twenty-five dollars ($25.00) per year for each renewal.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
775.06. Driver's badge.
   At the time a driver's license is issued, the Officer shall issue to the
driver a badge, the size and design of which shall be determined by the
Officer, upon which badge shall be inscribed and imprinted the word "chauffeur"
or the words "public vehicle operator," together with the number of such
license and the year in which it was issued. The badges shall be numbered
consecutively, and the number thereof shall correspond with the number of the
license issued to the driver.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
775.07. Badge to be worn when driving.
   Whenever a driver is driving any vehicle for which a license is required, he
shall wear his badge conspicuously and constantly upon such part of his cap or
outer garment as shall be designated by the Director or shall prominently
display the badge on the drivers side sun visor of the vehicle. No badge other
than that of the current driver shall be displayed at any time.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
775.08. Badge and driver's license nontransferable.
   Such badge and license shall not be assigned or transferred to any other
person.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
775.09. Lost badge.
   In case of the loss of a badge, the driver may file with the Director a
sworn statement containing the facts of such loss. The Director shall thereupon
notify the Officer who shall deliver a new badge to the driver upon payment of
five dollars ($5.00) for each replacement thereof.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
775.10. Identification card.
   At the time of the issuance of a license, the Officer shall also issue an
identification card upon which shall be affixed one of the photographs filed
with the Director. The identification card shall be carried at all times by the
licensee when he is driving a taxicab or motor vehicle for hire/limousine.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
775.11. Defacing of license certificate or badge prohibited.
   No licensed driver shall deface any license certificate, badge, tag,
identification card or rate cards or remove, tamper with or alter a rate card
displayed in a public vehicle.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
775.12. Expiration and renewal of public vehicle operator's license.
   Licenses as provided in this chapter shall expire on March 31 of the year
following that in which issued. Licenses must be renewed within thirty (30)
days after expiration; otherwise application must be made for a new license as
provided for original applicants. Applications for renewals shall be made to
the Director who may authorize renewals of licenses without further
examination, except for physical examinations which must comply with Section
775.02 and shall be furnished for renewal each even-numbered calendar year.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
775.13. New application after denial of license.
   When an applicant has been denied a license, no new application shall be
considered for a period of three (3) months.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
775.14. Marks for violation.
   For the purpose of regulating licensed drivers, the Director is authorized
to establish a system of violation marks for the violation of traffic
ordinances relating to public vehicles, in accordance with the following
classified schedule:
   (a)   Class I. Four violation marks shall be entered for each conviction of
any of the following offenses:
   (1)   Improper use of spotlight.
   (2)   Not having good brakes.
   (3)   Reckless driving.
   (4)   Speeding.
   (5)   Driving to the left of the center of street.
   (6)   Disobeying traffic light, voice or hand signals.
   (7)   Not giving name when requested.
   (8)   Not assisting at, stopping at or reporting accident.
   (9)   Not making main thoroughfare stops.
   (10)   Driving wrong way on one-way streets.
   (11)   Parking too close to fire hydrant.
   (12)   Operating a public vehicle without a permit, or with a suspended or
revoked permit.
   (13)   Not displaying metal tag.
   (14)   Improper or illegal manner of operation; illegal display of signs,
unjustified refusal to transport passengers.
   (15)   Use of unauthorized signs or advertising.
   (16)   Failure to display rate card.
   (17)   Not giving receipt when requested.
   (18)   Not using authorized zones.
   (19)   Parked within forbidden area, or over-time.
   (20)   Not having driver's license.
   (21)   Assigning, giving or transferring badge to another person.
   (22)   Driver of a public vehicle soliciting passengers on public property,
except as set forth in Section 779.03.
   (23)   Defacing identification card, badge or license certificate.
   (24)   Not stopping at unmarked railroad crossings.
   (b)   Class II. One (1) violation mark shall be entered for each conviction
under any traffic ordinance governing public vehicles not included in Class I.
Provided, however, that whenever a driver is fined costs, suspended, then no
violation marks shall be given, although the records shall be kept by the
Director.
   (c)   Class III. In addition to violation marks entered on convictions as
provided in Classes I and II, the Director may, after hearing, enter marks for
minor violation of rules and regulations, not exceeding one (1) mark in any
single case.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
775.15. Suspension for twelve violation marks.
   Whenever a licensed driver receives twelve (12) violation marks in
accordance with the schedule herein provided, during any twelve (12) month
period, it shall be mandatory upon the Director to suspend the license of the
driver for a period of thirty (30) days or for any period during which the
driver's state driver's license is suspended, whichever is longer.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
775.16. Suspension for intoxication and for driving while intoxicated.
   (a)   Conviction of driving while intoxicated shall result in a revocation
of any driver's license issued hereunder, and such driver shall not be eligible
to receive a new license for a period of one (1) year from the date of such
conviction.
   (b)   Any driver in charge of a taxicab or motor vehicle for hire/limousine
found on the public streets to be intoxicated and upon conviction for being
intoxicated while in charge of such taxicab or motor vehicle for hire/limousine
shall have his license suspended by the Director for a period of one (1) year
from the date of such conviction.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
775.17. Revocation mandatory.
   The Director shall revoke the license of any licensed driver for any of the
following reasons:
   (a)   Licensee having obtained a license by false statements in his
application, or upon misrepresentation or upon false statements on his
affidavits in applying for a duplicate badge.
   (b)   Licensee having become physically or mentally incapable of driving a
vehicle or upon information that any condition of the granting of the original
license is no longer true.
   (c)   Licensee having been convicted of any drug-related offense or of a
felony or misdemeanor involving moral turpitude.
   (d)   Licensee knowingly having directly or indirectly charged more than the
maximum or less than the minimum rate of fare fixed by this Public Vehicle
Code.
   (e)   Failure of licensee to lower flag or indicator on taxicab when such
taxicab is engaged for service.
   (f)   Upon information that unlawful use has occurred with the knowledge of
the person owning the public vehicle, or the knowledge of the operator of such
vehicle.
   (g)   Following conviction for violation of Section
783.14 it shall be mandatory for the Director to revoke the license of the
offender.
   (h)   No licensed driver shall deface any license certificate, badge, tag,
identification card or rate card, or remove, tamper with or alter a rate card
displayed in a public vehicle. In case of any violation of this provision the
Director shall revoke the driver's license. Such revocation shall be in
addition to any other penalty imposed.
   (i)   Conviction of driving while intoxicated shall operate as a revocation
of any driver's license issued hereunder and such driver shall not be eligible
to receive a new license for a period of one (1) year from the date of such
conviction.
   (j)   Whenever a licensed driver receives fifteen (15) violation marks in
any twelve (12) month period, it shall be mandatory upon the Director to revoke
the license of such driver, and such driver shall not be eligible to receive a
new license for a period of one (1) year from the date of such revocation.
   (k)   Whenever a licensed driver is convicted of driving a vehicle for which
a driver's license is required during a period for which his license has been
suspended, it shall be mandatory upon the Director to revoke the license of
such driver, and such driver shall not be eligible to receive a new license for
a period of one (1) year from the date of such revocation.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
775.18. Director of Public Safety to have continuing jurisdiction as to
licenses.
   The Director shall have continuing jurisdiction as to licenses granted
hereunder. In the event of misconduct or acts on the part of a licensed driver
that shows him to be a person unfit or unsuitable to drive a public vehicle, or
which would be sufficient to justify the refusal of a license in the case of an
original application, the Director shall revoke a license already granted. Any
such administrative revocation may be appealed to the Board of Review at its
next regular meeting.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
775.19. Notice regarding violations.
   The Chief of Police shall notify the Director, upon forms to be furnished by
the Director for that purpose, whenever any licensed driver is charged with or
convicted of the violation of any law or ordinance in such a manner as to
reflect on his moral character. In addition, the Chief of Police shall notify
the Director, upon forms to be furnished by the Director for that purpose, of
the conviction of any licensed driver for any violation of any ordinance
governing public vehicles, or of any traffic ordinance.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
775.20. Notice of suspension or revocation.
   The Director shall notify the driver of any suspension or revocation of his
license, and shall require such driver to turn in his certificate, license,
badge and identification card. Such notification shall be by registered mail or
by personal service, directed to the last address of the driver on file with
the Director.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
775.21. Change of address.
   Every licensed driver shall have his residence address on file with the
Director, and in case of change shall notify the Director in writing
immediately.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
775.99. Penalty.
   (a)   Any person, driver, owner, agent or employee who violates any of the
provisions of this chapter relative to license or driver's license, for which
no other fine and/or imprisonment is specified, shall be guilty of a minor
misdemeanor.
   (b)   No penalty (other than imposition of violation marks and suspensions
resulting therefrom as set forth in Toledo Municipal Code
Chapter 775) shall be imposed upon any person under this section, if such
person is punished for the same violation under the provisions of the Traffic
Code.
   (c)   Any person, firm or corporation or any owner, agent, employee, or
driver of a public vehicle who violates any of the provisions of this chapter,
for which no other fine and/or imprisonment is specified, shall be guilty of a
minor misdemeanor.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
CHAPTER 777

777.01. Liability insurance required.
   No permit to operate any taxicab or motor vehicle for hire/limousine under
this Public Vehicle Code, or any amendment thereto that shall hereafter be
made, shall be issued or renewed by the City unless and until the applicant has
filed with the Officer:
   A certificate signed by a duly authorized official of a company holding a
certificate of authority from the Ohio Department of Insurance and a member of
the Ohio Guarantee Fund to the effect that a policy of insurance covering the
vehicle(s) to be permitted has been issued to the applicant and is in full
force and effect, and that the premium has been paid as required thereon,
together with a true copy of the policy, contract or certificate of insurance.
In the event that there is no insurance company holding a "certificate of
authority" currently writing liability insurance for the taxicab or livery
business in the State of Ohio, the City may elect to accept a certificate of
insurance from an insurer who is approved by the Ohio Department of Insurance
to conduct excess and surplus lines business in Ohio and rated not less than
"A" by Best or other comparable insurance rating service. In cases where the
insurance premium is payable monthly, proper certificates or evidence of the
payment of the premiums for each month shall be delivered to the Officer not
later than the first of the month for which the premium is due and payable.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
777.02. Conditions of insurance policy.
   Such policy of insurance shall be conditioned for the payment of any
judgments recovered against such applicant whether person, firm, co-
partnership, corporation or association, for death or injuries to persons, or
damage to property, caused in the operation, maintenance or use or the
defective construction of the taxicab or motor vehicle for hire/limousine to be
issued a permit.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
777.03. Limit of automobile liability.
   Such policy of insurance shall provide that the limit of automobile
liability coverage shall be not less than the minimum amount specified for the
vehicle under the Ohio Revised Code or federal law, whichever is greater.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
777.04. Continued liability.
   Such policy of insurance shall contain a provision for a continuing
liability thereunder to the full amount thereof, notwithstanding any recovery
thereon, and until the policy is revoked, as herein provided, the insurance
company shall not be relieved from liability on account of nonpayment of
premium, failure to renew at the end of the year or any act or omission of the
named assured. Such policy of insurance shall be further conditioned for the
payment of any judgments up to the limits of such policy, recovered against any
person other than the owner, his agent or employee, who may operate the same
with the consent or acquiescence of the owner.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
777.05. Notice of intent to cancel or terminate.
   Any insurance company whose policy has been so filed pursuant to this
Chapter shall file a written notice with the Officer of its intention to
terminate and cancel such policy and give notice thereof to the named
applicant; whereupon after ten (10) days after such filing, such applicant or
owner shall cease to operate or cause to be operated within the City such
taxicab or motor vehicle for hire/limousine, and the permit issued therefor
shall be automatically revoked and liability on such policy shall cease and
terminate, provided that the liability of the insurance company thereon for any
act or omission of the applicant or owner occurring prior to the effective date
of cancellation shall not be thereby discharged or impaired.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
777.06. Policy to be filed with the Officer.
   No person shall operate any taxicab or motor vehicle for hire/limousine or
allow the same to be operated unless and until a policy of insurance in the
manner, to the extent and containing the provisions provided for in this
chapter has been filed with the Officer.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
777.99. Penalty.
   Any person or manager or director of a firm, partnership or corporation
operating a taxicab or motor vehicle for hire/limousine in violation of this
chapter is guilty of a misdemeanor of the fourth degree for each such offense.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)

Ch. 775
779.01. Consent of permit owner required.
   No taxicab or motor vehicle for hire/limousine shall be operated or driven
upon any street or highway without the consent of the owner of the permit.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
779.02. Limitation on use.
   Owners and drivers of taxicabs and motor vehicles for hire/limousines are
prohibited from causing or permitting such vehicles:
   (a)   To be operated over any regular route; except that the engagement of
such a vehicle by a specific customer to follow a prescribed route on a
recurring basis for purposes other than solicitation of business shall not
constitute a violation;
   (b)   To pass any specified point at regular intervals of time, or on any
fixed schedule;
   (c)   To be operated along any streetcar or bus route and soliciting by word
of mouth passengers from streetcar and bus stops; or
   (d)   When hired, to accept other passengers until the service for which it
has been hired is completed, unless requested by a passenger.
   Taxicabs and motor vehicles for hire/limousines shall at all times, when in
operation and not engaged, furnish service on demand to any orderly person for
lawful purposes.
   No person shall violate any of the provisions of this section and the
Director may suspend or revoke the permit or license of any owner or driver for
any such violation.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
779.03. Solicitation of passengers; Director may revoke driver's license.
   A driver or agent of the owner of any public vehicle for hire shall not
solicit passengers on public streets except by word of mouth in an ordinary
tone, or by motion of the hand, when standing beside such vehicle and shall not
solicit by word of mouth passengers from any street car or bus stop.
   No person shall violate any of the provisions of this section and the
Director may revoke the license of the driver or owner for such violation.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
779.04. Position of driver.
   The driver of any taxicab or motor vehicle for hire/limousine shall remain
in or alongside his vehicle at all times when such vehicle is standing upon the
public streets for hire.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
779.05. Number of passengers limited to seating capacity.
   No owner or driver of a taxicab or motor vehicle for hire/limousine shall
permit such vehicle to be occupied by more passengers than the number of the
actual seating capacity of such vehicle.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
779.06. Unauthorized passengers prohibited.
   (a)   Except as hereinafter provided, whenever any taxicab or motor vehicle
for hire/limousine is occupied by fare-paying passengers, or by members of the
party of a fare-paying passenger, the driver of such taxicab or motor vehicle
for hire/limousine shall permit no other person to occupy or ride in such
taxicab or motor vehicle for hire/limousine, except a supervisor or a student
driver to be schooled who has previously applied for a driver's license and
whose application is pending.
   It shall be permissible for a public vehicle already carrying one (1) or
more fare-paying passengers to admit additional passengers as long as all fare-
paying passengers to be carried at any one time are being transported pursuant
to a single contract with one third-party payer.
   (b)   Whenever any taxicab or motor vehicle for hire/limousine is unoccupied
or not completely occupied, the driver of such taxicab or motor vehicle for
hire/limousine shall permit no persons not intending to pay a fare to occupy or
ride in such taxicab or motor vehicle for hire/limousine, except a supervisor
or a student driver who has previously applied for a driver's license and whose
application is pending.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
779.07. Smoking prohibited.
   (a)   Smoking is prohibited in all taxicabs and motor vehicles for hire/
limousines at all times, including when the vehicle is not in service.
   (b)   Signage to this effect shall be prominently displayed in each taxicab
and motor vehicle for hire/limousine.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
779.08. Body light.
   Every public vehicle shall be equipped with operable lights within the
passenger compartment of the vehicle.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
779.09. Safety or shatterproof glass.
   Every public vehicle shall have safety or shatterproof glass in its
windshield, windows, doors and partitions. Provided, however, that public
vehicles not equipped with such partition or solid front seat, or with safety
or shatterproof glass, as provided for herein, shall be permitted to continue
operation if they were lawfully in service on the date of passage of this
section and otherwise the conditions of this section shall be complied with.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
779.10. Advertising and signs on public vehicles.
   The display of general advertising material is permitted on taxicabs and
motor vehicles for hire/limousines as follows:
   (a)   Semi-transparent film or wrap is permitted on the rear-seat side
windows or the vehicle's rear window.
   (b)   Opaque lettering/design is permitted on the top of the front
windshield or the top or bottom (but not both) of the rear window if it does
not extend more than four (4) inches from the respective edge of the window
glass.
   (c)   No lettering or design shall obstruct any safety equipment including
the rear-window-mounted brake light.
   (d)   A roof-mounted sign with a maximum height of eighteen (18) inches,
including bracket, is permitted.
   (e)   Advertising material may be displayed on the body panels of the
vehicle with the prior approval of the Board of Review.
   The Board of Review shall retain final authority for approval or disapproval
of any advertising material.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
779.11. Record of vehicles and drivers.
   The owner or person in charge of one or more taxicabs or motor vehicles for
hire/limousines shall keep a record of all such public vehicles showing the
body number, the City permit number and such data as may be necessary to
identify the driver of such vehicle or vehicles at any and all times.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
779.12. Record of trips made.
   Such owner or person in charge shall also keep a record of the trips made,
giving the time of departures from starting point, and arrival at the
destination, garage or headquarters of each taxicab or motor vehicle for hire/
limousine. Such records shall be subject to inspection at all times by the
Police Division and by the Director.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
779.13. Records to be kept sixty days.
   Such records shall be kept for a period of sixty (60) days. Any owner or
driver of a taxicab or motor vehicle for hire/limousine who fails to keep a
record as aforesaid or who falsifies the record shall be deemed guilty of a
violation of this chapter and subject to the penalty hereinafter provided.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
779.14. Articles left in vehicles.
   Drivers of public vehicles shall promptly notify the Police Division of all
items of property in excess of twenty-five dollars ($25.00) in value left in
such vehicles by passengers.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
779.15. Passenger carrying for hire by other vehicles prohibited.
   The carrying of passengers as a business for compensation by any vehicle
other than a public vehicle, duly permitted under and operating in accordance
with the provisions of this Public Vehicle Code, operating under proper
authority, is hereby prohibited, providing, however, that nothing within the
meaning of this section shall be construed to prohibit motor buses or omnibuses
from the carrying of passengers as a business for compensation.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
779.16. Vehicles from other cities.
   Public vehicles having no Toledo permit and whose place of business is not
in the City of Toledo may bring passengers into Toledo and return the same
passenger(s) to a destination outside Toledo but may not pick up any other
passengers, for any destination, or accept any other business, within the City
of Toledo.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
779.99. Penalty.
   (a)   Any person who uses a public vehicle for any illegal purpose is guilty
of a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.
   (b)   Whoever, with intent to defraud the owner or driver of any public
vehicle, engages carriage therein is guilty of a misdemeanor of the fourth
degree. Refusal to pay the lawful charge for such carriage, or absconding
without payment or offer to pay shall be evidence of such intent to defraud.
   (c)   Any person, firm or corporation, or any owner, agent, employee or
driver of a public vehicle who violates any of the provisions of this chapter
for which no other fine and/or imprisonment is specified is guilty of a minor
misdemeanor.
(Ord. 304-08. Passed 10-7-08.)
