RECOGNITION
2123.01 Recognition.
   (A)    This Agreement is made and entered into by and between AFSCME Ohio
Council 8, Local 7, AFL-CIO (hereinafter referred to as the Union) and the City
of Toledo Department of Health and Environment (hereinafter referred to as the
City).
   (B)    The purpose, of this Agreement is to maintain an orderly system of
employer-employee relations, which will facilitate joint discussions and
cooperative solutions of mutual problems by the City and representatives of its
Public Health Nurse employees included in the bargaining unit. The City and
AFSCME Local 7 further recognize their common interest beyond the collective
bargaining relationship, and both pledge to strive together to insure the
highest quality of health service and the highest standards of professional
nursing care and practice.
   (C)    Pursuant to the Certification of Representative issued by the State
of Ohio Employment Relations Board dated September 24, 1998, Case Number 98-
REP-08-0176, the City of Toledo recognizes AFSCME Ohio Council 8, Local 7 as
the sole and exclusive representative for those classifications of Public
Health Nurses employed by the City of Toledo Department of Health and
Environment and included in the bargaining unit for the purposes of collective
bargaining with respect to wages, hours, working conditions and other matters
of mutual concern relating thereto. The registered nurse classification
included in this bargaining unit is Public Health Nurse.
   (D)    As used herein the term "Public Health Nurse" or "nurse" shall
designate a member of the bargaining unit. The term "bargaining unit" shall be
understood to include all Public Health Nurses in the classification referenced
in Section (C) above who are employed by the City Department of Health and
Environment.
   (E)    Each person employed by the City to practice professional nursing
must be registered and licensed to practice such in the State of Ohio.
   (F)    Professional services normally and traditionally rendered by Public
Health Nurses shall continue to be performed by Public Health Nurses in
accordance with the Nurse Practice Act of the State of Ohio; and said services
shall neither be assigned to nor performed by other employees.
MANAGEMENT RIGHTS
2123.02 Management rights.
   AFSCME Local 7 recognizes that the management of the City of Toledo, its
business, properties and facilities, and the direction of the nursing staff is
vested exclusively in the City. These rights shall include but not be limited
to, the right to plan, direct, and control operations and procedures; to
schedule work, subcontract work, establish job qualifications, work
assignments, transfers and any other matters necessary for the conduct of its
operations and business; to hire, discipline or discharge employees for just
cause; to determine the number and classification of employees to be employed;
to determine the number of employees in any classification; to introduce new or
improved methods or facilities and to make and enforce reasonable rules for the
efficient conduct of its business and the maintenance of the discipline and
efficiency of the working force and to perform such duties in a non-capricious
and arbitrary manner. Any discharge or disciplinary action must be reasonable
and for just cause. The City specifically reserves all rights except those as
may be altered by agreement herein.
AFSCME LOCAL 7 REPRESENTATION
2123.03 AFSCME Local 7 representation.
   (A)    The Union shall be represented by one (1) Union Steward and one (1)
alternate Union Steward and shall furnish their names to the Department of
Human Resources and the Department of Health and Environment.
   (B)    The Union Steward shall be permitted reasonable time during working
hours to investigate and process grievances raised by bargaining unit members
and to represent members in disciplinary actions brought by management. The
Union Steward shall notify their immediate supervisors that they are leaving
their jobs to handle a problem and shall report when returning to work
utilizing the designated form. The Union Steward shall also be permitted
reasonable time to conduct other necessary union business during working hours.
In the absence of the Union Steward, the alternate will be allowed to assume
the duties of the Union Steward.
   It is the intent of the parties that union release time will be utilized in
the manner that will least interfere with City operations.
   (C)    An authorized representative of the Union shall have the right to
visit the premises during working hours for valid purposes relating to this
Agreement, including the processing of grievances and meeting with management
representatives in matters relating to this Agreement. Such representative
shall notify the office of the Director of Health and Environment prior to
entering the premises and shall abide by reasonable regulations of the
Department.
   (D)    Employees elected to the Executive Board of the union shall be
allowed time off without pay or may use their personal or vacation time to
attend meetings and/or conferences.
   (E)    Employees appointed or elected to a union position or office shall be
granted a leave of absence not to exceed one (1) year.
   (F)    The Union shall be permitted to conduct a monthly meeting of all
nurses in the bargaining unit for a period of up to thirty (30) minutes. This
meeting shall be held either at the beginning or at the end of the work day on
the premises, and shall be scheduled by mutual consent.
DUES DEDUCTION
2123.04 Dues deduction.
   (A)    In recognition of the Union's services to the bargaining unit and to
promote harmonious and stable relationships between the bargaining unit and the
Department of Health and Environment, employees within the bargaining unit
shall, within thirty (30) days of this agreement, or their completion of their
probationary period, whichever is later, either become members of the Union or
share in the financial support of AFSCME Local 7 by paying to the organization
a fair share fee not to exceed the amount of the dues uniformly required of
members of the organization.
   (B)    The City will deduct any unpaid Union dues, current Union dues,
special fees and Fair Share Fees from the paychecks of employees working in the
classification included in the recognition clause herein, who have signed the
proper authorization card, authorizing such deductions from the paychecks of
the employee. Such deductions shall be made from the first paycheck of the
month for which current dues are due the Union. The City further agrees to
remit to the Union, all Union dues and fees so deducted from the paychecks of
the employees covered herein.
   (C)    The City shall be relieved from making such checkoff deductions upon
(a) termination of employment, (b) transfer to a job other than one covered by
the bargaining unit, (c) layoff from work, (d) leave of absence, or (e)
revocation of the checkoff authorization in accordance with its terms or with
applicable law.
   (D)    The City shall not be obliged to make dues deductions of any kind
from any employee who, during any dues month involved, shall have failed to
receive sufficient wages to equal the dues deductions.
   (E)    The Union shall indemnify and save the City of Toledo harmless
against any liability that may arise out of, or by reason of, any actions taken
by the City for the purpose of complying with the provisions of this section.
In the event that the City is held to be responsible for the repayment of
monies paid to the Union pursuant to this section, the Union to the extent of
those funds actually received, shall reimburse same to the City and/or the
designated employees involved.
PLEDGE AGAINST DISCRIMINATION AND COERCION
2123.05 Pledge against discrimination and coercion.
   (A)    The provisions herein shall be applied equally to all employees
without discrimination as to age, sex, marital status, race, color, creed,
national origin, handicap, or political affiliation. The failure of the City to
apply provisions herein without discrimination, when brought to the attention
of the Bargaining Agent, shall be subject to the provisions of the grievance
procedure.
   (B)    Particularly, it is the express intent of the parties that this
agreement shall not be interpreted in such a manner as to cause or constitute a
violation of any law, specifically including Title VII of PL-88-352, as
amended, known as the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and the Civil Rights Act of
1991.
   (C)    All references to employees in this Agreement designate both sexes.
   (D)    Further it is the intent of the parties to provide a work environment
free from any sexual harassment. Remedies for any alleged sexual harassment
shall be in accordance with Administrative Policy #34 provided, however, that
any remedy for violation of this shall be as set forth therein or provided by
law.
   (E)    The City agrees not to interfere with the rights of employee(s) to
become members of the Union, and there shall be no discrimination,
interference, restraint, or coercion by the City or its representatives against
any legal employee activity in an official capacity on behalf of the Union.
   (F)    The Union recognizes its responsibility and agrees to represent all
employee(s) in the Union without discrimination, interference, restraint, or
coercion. The Union agrees not to intimidate or coerce any employee in an
effort to recruit membership in the Union.
   (G)    Both parties recognize the need for an Affirmative Action Program and
agree to cooperate in the implementation of the program of the City as
established by ordinance and administrative regulation.
SENIORITY AND ROTATION OF NURSES
2123.06 Seniority.
   (A)    Seniority is defined as the length of time in service by a registered
nurse in the City's employ and such seniority shall be broken only as provided
for in Section D of this Article. Those nurses hired under the former Board of
Health will maintain their original seniority date of hire in effect when the
Health Department was placed under the City operation.
   (B)    Nurses hired on the City payroll who have prior service with any
political subdivision of the State of Ohio shall be credited for vacation and
any accrued sick leave benefits earned.
   (C)    Position openings in classification covered by this Agreement shall
be posted by administration on the Union bulletin board and in other areas for
not less than one (1) calendar week before being permanently filled from the
bargaining unit. The position shall be awarded (notification) within one (1)
calendar week after the end of the posting period. If no nurse applies from the
bargaining unit during the one (1) calendar week posting time, the City may go
outside the unit to fill the position. Copies of the posting shall be provided
to the Union local unit representative at the time it is posted, and copies of
the award shall also be provided to the Union local unit representative at the
same time the successful bidder is notified. An employee must have completed
six (6) months of service after the most recent probationary period to be
eligible to bid to another job, except as agreed to by both parties.
   An employee who accepts a bid to another job shall be probationary for a
period of two hundred forty (240) actual hours worked. During this period,
either the City or the employee can request movement of the employee back to
their former position. If the employee's former position has been filled, the
employee filling that position may be removed and reinstated to their former
position.
   Job selection will be based on qualifications, disciplines, and attendance;
with all things being equal, seniority shall control. In the event that the
most senior nurse is bypassed, he/she may dispute reason(s) for being bypassed
to the Director of the Department of Health and Environment.
   (D)    A nurse shall be given written notice of the reason for loss of
seniority; when under Paragraphs (4) and (5), the loss of seniority shall be
subject to a review by the Department of Human Resources. Seniority of the
nurse shall be considered broken and the nurse shall be terminated for the
following reasons:
      1.    The nurse resigns her position in the service.
      2.    The nurse is discharged for just cause and the discharge is
sustained.
      3.    After recall notice has been sent to the nurse and the nurse fails
to report for work after fourteen (14) calendar days.
      4.    The nurse is absent on her own accord for a period of more than
five (5) consecutive work days, and fails to apply for a leave of absence.
      5.    The nurse fails to return at the expiration of an approved leave of
absence.
      6.    A nurse enters employment for another employer or becomes self-
employed while on leave.
      7.    A nurse is laid off continuously for more than two (2) years.
2123.07 Rotation of nurses.
   The nurse rotation list shall include all bargaining unit nurses from the
clinic.
   Nurses on the list may be assigned as replacement for absent nurses or to
supplement staffing as necessary from available nurses by rotation in the
following order:
      (1)   Voluntary - nurses on list of volunteers.
      (2)   In the event the volunteer list is exhausted, then by seniority
qualification considered, and then in inverse order.
   A rotation is considered to be for a minimum time period of four (4)
consecutive hours. A nurse off work or bypassed when his/her rotation occurs
will be placed in the rotation of the next lower nurse required to work in his/
her absence. No nurse will be assigned for more than three consecutive days
except by mutual agreement by the nurse and management.
   When it is known in advance that an employee will be required to work as a
replacement for an extended period of time, the schedule will be posted by
supervision by the end of the shift on Thursday prior to the week the vacancy
exists.
PROBATIONARY PERIOD--ORIENTATION PERIOD
2123.08 Probationary period.
   (A)    Newly employed nurses shall be considered to be on probation for a
period of six (6) months, starting from their date of employment. The
probationary period may be extended by mutual agreement of the City and the
Union.
   (B)    During the probationary period, a nurse shall have no seniority
rights but, at the end of the period, seniority shall be computed from the date
of employment. Any discipline or dismissal during the probationary period shall
not be grievable.
   (C)    All newly hired nurses will be placed into a program and will not be
allowed to transfer out for a six month period unless mutually agreed to by the
Administration and the Union. Probationary nurses shall not be included on the
rotation list until after the completion of the probationary period.
   (D)    A probationary nurse shall not be eligible for fringe benefits during
the first sixty (60) calendar days of the probationary period.
2123.09 Orientation.
   (A)    An orientation program for newly employed nurses shall include but
not be limited to content covering the clinic areas. The orientation program
will be directed by the Nurse Supervisor, the purpose of which is to provide
all nursing personnel the ability to work within the clinic areas. Unit nurses
may be required to assist in training a new nurse. At the end of the
orientation program, the nurse will receive an evaluation, which shall serve as
the basis for supervision and assistance and periodic evaluation during the
balance of the nurse's probation period. The length of the orientation period
should normally be four (4) weeks, but may be more or less depending on a newly
employed nurse's training and experience.
   (B)    A probationary nurse shall not be eligible for fringe benefits during
the first sixty (60) calendar days of the probationary period.
LAYOFF AND RECALL PROCEDURES
2123.10 Layoff procedures.
   When the City determines a layoff will be necessary, they shall notify the
Union Steward(s) and President the number of bargaining unit members affected.
   (B)    The layoff notice shall be at least 30 days in advance of the layoff.
   (C)    The order of the layoff shall be as follows:
      1.    Any person who volunteers in the group;
      2.    Any newly hired probationary nurse in the group;
      3.    Any regularly employed nurse in the group beginning with the least
senior nurse.
   (D)    Layoff notices will be served on employees scheduled for layoff. If
an employee is absent from work, then the layoff notice will be sent to the
employee's last known address by certified mail. A copy will be sent to the
union President.
2123.11 Recall procedure.
   (A)    Bargaining unit members shall be offered recall in the order of
seniority. A laid off employee will retain recall rights for 48 months.
   (B)    A laid off employee offered recall shall notify the employer within
14 days of their intent to return to work and must be able to work within 14
calendar days of receipt of such notice. Failure to follow the time frames set
forth will constitute a voluntary resignation.
   (C)    Recall notice will be sent to the employee by certified mail to the
employee's last recorded address. A copy will be sent to the union President.
OUTSIDE EMPLOYMENT, REVIEW OF PERSONNEL RECORDS, AND AGENCY NURSE
2123.12 Outside employment.
   No nurse employed by the City shall accept outside employment that is
adverse to or in conflict with the nurse's employment with the City. In the
event a nurse shall be injured while engaged in outside employment, the nurse
shall not be entitled to any sick leave benefits which may have been
accumulated by virtue of his/her employment by the City.
2123.13 Review of personnel records.
   A nurse shall have the right to review his/her personnel records by
appointment. No part of the record may be removed during the nurse's review,
but a copy of any document within the file shall be made available to the nurse
upon request at no charge.
TERMINATION OF EMPLOYMENT AND DISCIPLINE
2123.14 Termination of employment.
   (A)    Any employee whose removal from the service is sought for
disciplinary reasons may resign at any time and the record shall show that the
employee resigned of the employee's own accord.
   Any employee who wishes to leave the City service in good standing shall
sign a written resignation with the Director of Health and Environment or
designee at least two (2) weeks in advance of the date the employee wishes the
resignation to be effective.
   Employees planning to retire should provide notice of their anticipated
approximate retirement date the year before the retirement is planned.
   (B)    Any nurse who leaves the employ of the City may be afforded the
opportunity for an exit interview.
   (C)    Nurses who terminate employment with the City of Toledo for any
reason or who retire or die while in employment with the City of Toledo shall
receive compensation for any unused vacation accumulation, unused compensatory
time, unused holiday credit, including discretionary holiday(s), prorated
longevity pay for months worked in that year. And, in case of retirement, as
defined by the Public Employees' Retirement System, or death, severance pay for
unused sick time shall be provided in accordance with the provisions of Section
2123.36, Sick Days Accumulation.
2123.15 Discipline.
   (A)    The City shall maintain the right to discipline or to discharge any
nurse employed within its jurisdiction for just cause. When it becomes
necessary to discipline an employee, management will administer the procedure
based on whether the employee's actions require a verbal warning, written
warning, suspension or dismissal. The application of the steps is contingent
upon the type and occurrence of the various offenses.
   The City will notify the President or designee of AFSCME Local 7 immediately
of any discharge or suspension of any nurse covered by this Agreement. Said
notification will be confirmed in writing to the Union President, with a copy
mailed to AFSCME Local 7.
   (B)    No nurse shall be discharged, suspended, or taken out of service
without a preliminary hearing and consultation with the Mayor or designee,
except where necessary to immediately take the nurse out of service pending a
hearing, as determined by the Mayor or designee. The preliminary hearing shall
be held by the Mayor or designee as soon as practical, and the presence of the
charging party shall be required. Following the preliminary hearing on a
suspension or temporary removal from service or discharge, the decision of the
Mayor or designee shall be rendered in writing within seven (7) working days.
   (C)    A nurse shall have the right to request one Union Steward at all
stages of the procedures provided in this Section.
   (D)    Any action taken against a nurse shall be subject to the appeal
procedure of the Civil Service Commission or the grievance procedure provided
herein at the option of the nurse. Where a nurse has elected to file a
grievance in accordance with Section
2123.16 herein, and subsequently files an appeal to the Civil Service
Commission, then the grievance shall be considered to be dismissed.
GRIEVANCE PROCEDURE
2123.16 Recognized levels and definition.
   (A)    The recognized levels of management under the grievance procedure are
as follows: the operational unit, the Division or Agency, and the Department of
Human Resources.
   (B)    Definitions. Disputes involving interpretation, application, or
enforcement of the terms of this agreement shall constitute a grievance under
the provisions set forth herein.
2123.17 Grievance steps.
   Step 1. A nurse having a grievance, shall present a written grievance to the
immediate supervisor within five (5) work days after the existence of the
dispute is known to the nurse. The supervisor shall render a written response
by five (5) work days after receipt of a grievance. If the grievance is not
resolved with the supervisor, the grievance may be appealed to Step 2.
   Step 2. If the grievance is not satisfactorily resolved at Step 1 of this
procedure, the grievance may be submitted in writing, dated, and signed, to the
Director of Health and Environment within seven (7) working days after the
answer from Step 1 has been received. The Director of Health and Environment or
a designated representative shall meet with the grievant, Union Steward, and a
member of the Committee within ten (10) working days of receipt of the
grievance for discussion purposes. The Director of Health and Environment shall
give the answer in writing within ten (10) working days after the hearing.
   Step 3. If the grievance is not satisfactorily resolved at Step 2 of this
procedure, the grievance matter may be submitted in writing, dated, and signed,
to the Department of Human Resources within seven (7) working days after the
answer from Step 2 is received. The Department of Human Resources shall
schedule a hearing to take place at a mutually agreeable time, not to exceed
ten (10) workdays from receipt of the appeal of Step 2. The Department of Human
Resources shall give an answer in writing within ten (10) working days after
the hearing.
   Step 4. If the grievance is not resolved at Step 3 of this procedure, then
the grievance matter may be submitted at the request of the Union for
arbitration by a notification in writing to the Director of Human Resources
within ten (10) working days after the receipt of written answer to Step 3. If
the parties cannot agree to an impartial arbitrator, one shall be selected by
the "odd man remaining procedure" from a panel of at least seven (7)
individuals to be supplied by the Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service.
The arbitrator shall have the jurisdiction only over disputes arising out of
grievances as defined herein. The arbitrator shall not add to, subtract from,
or modify any of the provisions, terms or conditions of this Agreement. The
decision of the arbitrator shall be final and binding on the City, the Union,
and the nurse in matters pertaining to the particular grievance involved. The
fee and expenses of the arbitrator shall be borne by the losing party. Each
party shall pay the cost of its own copy of the transcript of the record, if
ordered. The arbitrator shall render his decision in writing within thirty (30)
days after the close of the hearing.
2123.18 Failure to answer or appeal.
   Any time limitations within the procedure may be extended by mutual
agreement of the City and the Union. Any resolution of a grievance reached at
any step of this procedure shall be binding on the City, the Union, and the
nurse in matters pertaining to the particular grievance involved. Any grievance
not presented or appealed within the time limits stated herein at any step
shall be considered no grievance. In the absence of the required response on
the part of management within the time authorized at any step of this
procedure, it shall be understood that the grievance has been resolved in favor
of the grievant.
2123.19 Grievance acceleration.
   A grievance which affects a substantial number of nurses or which involves
the disciplinary suspension or discharge of a nurse may initially be presented
at Step 2 of Section
2123.17 if presented within the time limit specified in Step 1.
2123.20 Grievance investigation.
   The Union shall be permitted reasonable time to investigate and process
grievances and conduct other necessary business during working hours. The Union
Steward must receive prior approval by the Director of Health or designee and
said investigation must not disrupt the normal business activities of the
Health Department.
EDUCATION AND TUITION REIMBURSEMENT
2123.21 Education.
   The City agrees that all nurses covered by the terms of this Agreement may
participate in continuing education programs.
2123.22 In service education.
   The Department may provide monthly in-service education programs, and will
receive suggestions for such programs from the bargaining unit.
2123.23 Tuition reimbursement.
   The City shall reimburse tuition costs for job-related courses taken at an
educationally accredited college or university by full-time permanent
employees. Such course work must be approved as job-related prior to enrolling
by submitting a description of the course to the employee's Division Head.
Thereafter, the course work must be approved by the Department Head and finally
by the Director of Human Resources.
   The City shall reimburse eighty percent (80%) for a grade of "C", ninety
percent (90%) for a grade of "B", or one hundred percent (100%) for a grade of
"A". The City will reimburse the appropriate percentage of the cost of tuition
only for ten (10) credit hours per quarter. These costs will be reimbursed upon
the documented presentation of a "C" or 2.0 grade or better.
Non-accredited schools will be included, if job related.
HOURS OF WORK AND OVERTIME
2123.24 Work schedule.
   The work week shall consist of forty (40) hours of work performed in five
(5) eight (8) hour shifts, starting at 8:00 a.m. and ending at 4:45 p.m. Monday
through Friday of the same week.
   After the effective date of this Agreement in the event an existing position
is vacated or a new position created, the starting time and days to be worked
may be adjusted by the City to accommodate an effective delivery of service.
   Said changes in starting time and/or days will be noted on the position
posting.
2123.25 Breaks.
   Nurses will be allowed two (2) fifteen-minute breaks during each workday,
one break to be taken during each half-day work period.
2123.26 Lunch.
   Nurses will be allowed a period of forty-five (45) minutes for lunch without
pay. Nurses may combine a break period with a lunch period if taken between 11:
00 a.m. and 2:00 p.m. with prior approval of the supervisor. In the event of a
circumstance which precludes a nurse from taking her lunch period between these
hours, the nurse will contact her supervisor before taking her lunch period.
2123.27 Charting.
   In order to provide the necessary time to perform properly the duties of
their classification, nurses will not routinely be asked to assume
responsibilities outside their classification.
2123.28 Evening meetings.
   When a nurse attends an evening meeting as part of his/her work assignment,
the nurse will be reimbursed for actual time worked at the appropriate overtime
rate, including travel time in both directions, with prior approval in writing
from his/her supervisor. A nurse required to attend a meeting contiguous to the
shift will receive overtime pay for the time worked without travel time.
2123.29 Overtime.
   (A)    Except as provided elsewhere in this Agreement, nurses shall be paid
one and one-half (1-1/2) times their regular straight time rate of pay for all
hours worked in excess of eight (8) hours in any one workday or in excess of
forty (40) hours in any one workweek.
   (B)    Nurses who are assigned to work weekends shall be paid at the rate of
one and one-half (1-1/2) times their regular rate of pay for all hours worked
on Saturdays and at the rate of two (2) times their regular rate of pay for all
hours worked on Sundays (provided such nurses have been credited with forty
(40) hours straight time pay in the work week).
   (C)    An employee who has worked overtime may at the discretion of the
Division/ Department Head elect to receive time off in lieu of pay at the
appropriate overtime rate, provided that the employee does not accumulate
compensatory time in excess of Fair Labor Standards Act limitations. The
application hereof shall be applied uniformly and shall not be arbitrarily or
capriciously withheld. They shall receive this time off with pay in such a way
as not to impair the operations of the work unit.
   In the absence of such election, the employee shall receive pay as provided
herein.
   In the event an employee, due to the nature of their job or work schedule,
is prohibited from scheduling compensatory time off, said employee may elect to
receive a compensatory pay-out of any amount of their banked compensatory time
with any payroll.
   An employee must take all compensatory time in excess of eighty (80) hours
by April 30 of the year following the year in which the time was earned. If the
employee has not taken the time by that date, then that employee shall be paid
for all hours not taken in excess of eighty (80) hours in the next regular pay
period.
   (D)    A nurse who is assigned to work on Saturday or Sunday shall be
guaranteed four (4) hours' pay at the appropriate premium rate on any weekend
day worked.
   Overtime will first be offered to the nurse assigned to the program
requiring overtime. In the event the nurse assigned to the area declines the
overtime, such overtime will be offered to the remaining nurses in the
respective unit on the basis of seniority according to a rotating list. When it
is necessary to assign overtime, it shall be assigned by inverse order of
seniority according to a rotating list.
WAGE RATES AND ALLOWANCES
2123.30 Wage rates.
   (A)    Effective July 1, 1997, employees shall receive two and one-half
percent (2.5%) increase in the wage rates which became effective July 1, 1996,
as follows:
 
                        Full Rate 5-Year Rate
Rates effective 7/1/96: $17.688   $18.744
Rates effective 7/1/97: $18.130   $19.213
 
   (B)    Effective July 1, 1998, the foregoing rate will be increased by three
percent (3.0%), as follows:
 
                        Full Rate 5 Year Rate
Rates effective 7/1/98: $18.674   $19.789
 
   (C)    The July 1, 1997 and July 1, 1998 rates shown above shall not become
payable until April 1, 1999.
   (D)    Nurses hired on or after January 1, 1993 that are not placed from
within City of Toledo employment will be paid at the Step Rate of the salary
provided in this Section as follows:
 
1st Year 85% of Full Rate
2nd Year 90% of Full Rate
3rd Year 95% of Full Rate
4th Year 100% of Full Rate
 
   (E)    Effective July 1, 1994, the City will pay three-tenths of one percent
(0.3%) of each individual employee's 8.5% pension contribution (employee
payment reduced from 8.5% to 8.2%) in lieu of the employee paying the same.
   Effective July 1, 1995, the City will pay three-tenths of one percent (0.3%)
of each individual employee's pension contribution (employee payment reduced
from 8.2% to 7.9%) in lieu of the employee paying the same.
   Effective July 1, 1996, the City will pay four-tenths of one percent (0.4%)
of each individual employee's pension contribution (employee payment reduced
from 7.9% to 7.5%) in lieu of the employee paying the same.
   Effective July 1, 1997, the City will pay one half of one percent (0.5%) of
each individual employee's pension contribution (employee payment reduced from
7.5% to 7.0%) in lieu of the employee paying the same.
   Effective July 1, 1998, the City will pay one percent (1.0%) of each
individual employee's pension contribution (employee payment reduced from 7.0%
to 6.0%) in lieu of the employee paying the same.
   The City's P.E.R.S. payment for the period from July 1, 1997 through April
1, 1999 shall be paid to the employee as a lump sum, from which no P.E.R.S.
deductions or contributions shall be made. The City's actual payment of the
contribution specified for July 1, 1997 and July 1, 1998 shall not become
effective until April 1, 1999.
   Effective April 1, 1999, employees will not receive P.E.R.S. payment
directly; the payments will be made to P.E.R.S. employee individual
contribution account.
   (F)    The City shall provide a one-time lump sum payment of $3,000.00 to
each eligible full time bargaining unit member and $1,500.00 to each eligible
half-time bargaining unit member in the unit as of February 24, 1999 which
includes the lump sum specified in paragraph (E) above and the wage increases
specified in (A) and (B) above.
2123.31 Longevity pay.
   (A)    Regular nurses appointed prior to June 1, 1985, shall be entitled to
and be paid longevity in accordance with the following formula:
 
CALENDAR YEAR OF CONTINUOUS SERVICE PERCENT OF ANNUAL BASE HOURLY RATE
After 5 years                       2%
After 10 years                      4%
After 15 years                      6%
After 20 years                      8%
   (B)    An employee shall receive a pro rata percentage based on the portion
of the calendar year in which the employee reaches the plateau of years of
service as set forth above at the appropriate rate indicated.
   (C)    The longevity hourly base rates revised effective January 1, 1983,
shall be used in computing each employee's longevity payment. No further
increases are to result from any cost of living or other increase in the base
rate during the life of this agreement.

   (D)    The longevity payment shall be made in a separate check to be
distributed to the nurses on the first payday in December of the year for which
payment is being made.
2123.32 Supplemental pay.
   A thirty cents ($.30) per hour supplement will be paid to the nurse who
works in the Sexually Transmitted Disease Clinic.
VACATION AND HOLIDAYS
2123.33 Vacation.
   (A)    Employees of the City shall be entitled to annual vacation with pay
based upon their cumulative length of continuous service as follows:
 
Length of Service                    Accumulated Vacation
Less than one (1) full calendar year .916 days for each full month
After 1 full calendar year           2 weeks
After 7 full calendar years          3 weeks
After 14 full calendar years         4 weeks
After 21 full calendar years         5 weeks
After 25 full calendar years         6 weeks
   (B)    In determining eligibility for vacation, only continuous years of
service shall be counted.
   (C)    An employee should take vacation in the calendar year following the
year in which it was earned. In the event an employee is not allowed to
schedule their vacation in the year in which it should have been taken, they
may request that such unused vacation be carried over to the following year.
Such request must be submitted to the Department of Human Resources prior to
December 1 of each year. All such carry over vacation must be taken no later
than April 30 of the following year.
   (D)    An employee shall not be allowed to be paid cash in lieu of receiving
vacation unless the City for some valid reason has not allowed the employee to
take the vacation time to which he is entitled by April 30 of the year
following the calendar year in which it should have been taken. In that event,
the employee shall be paid for such unused vacation days.
   (E)    If a holiday listed in Section
2123.34 of this Agreement falls within a nurse's vacation, the nurse shall be
permitted at her option to take an additional day with pay at the beginning or
end of her vacation, or at another mutually agreeable date.
   (F)    Nurses who regularly work half time or more, but less than full time,
shall earn paid vacation time on a pro-rated basis.
   (G)    The Department will provide a list showing the vacation and holiday
accumulation of each nurse.
   (H)    The vacation calendar for the 12-month period January 1 December 31
will be posted by January 1 of the year and granting of vacation time shall be
by seniority, until April 1 of the year for the 12-month period January 1 -
December 31.
   The Department will determine the number of employees per unit who may take
vacation during any given period of time. Any vacation not selected during the
January 1 - April 1 period will then be granted on a first come, first served
basis. In the case of a dispute, vacation request shall continue to be granted
on the basis of seniority.
   The Department will respond to such request by April 15 when requested
between January 1 and April 1 and within fourteen (14) days of any request
thereafter.
   (I)    On termination of employment, a nurse shall receive vacation pay for
which she is eligible.
   (J)    A nurse may make a request for a maximum of five (5) days' pay at the
time of vacation. The request must be made to the payroll clerk at least
fourteen (14) calendar days prior to the payday on which the check is to be
received. This procedure is contingent on the employee having worked in the
period sufficient to be entitled to the advance pay requested.
   (K)    Nurses covered by this Agreement shall be given bonus days providing
the nurse has earned sick pay benefits in the previous year in accordance with
the Bonus Day Table as follows:
